Home page: stacked blocks → a grid you can compare down

Before: your VS Code browser pane (~1080px wide) fell under the old 1200px breakpoint, so every app was a separate block and no column lined up. After: the same width is a real table.

What moved

  1. GRID The table now stays a table down to 641px. Stacked blocks are for phones only (640px and below).
  2. SCROLL When the eight columns don't fit, the card scrolls sideways and the app column stays pinned on the left, with a hairline marking the edge.
  3. SHORT Every cell is a one-line label ("Table + Blob", "Azure OpenAI", "PWA", "App Service · Linux"), so a column reads at a glance and rows stay the same height.
  4. HINT A cell with a dotted underline has more to say: hover, tap or focus it for the full wording ("Azure OpenAI: GPT-5 mini judges, GPT-4o mini TTS speaks"). Screen readers get that text inline.
  5. KEPT The thumbnail, name, description, Down badge and streak stay in the app column.
  6. DATA Each stack block in apps.json now holds short values plus a details map. Hosting's detail ("Azure App Service on Linux, free tier (F1)") comes from the scan.
